tutorial.title: JavaScript Libraries
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn the basics of including and using Libraries via CDN

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
A library stores books and allows us to borrow them. You can even donate books you want to share with others.

There are libraries in JavaScript too! We can borrow code written by others and also contribute with our code for others to use.

lessons.title: Library
lessons.interactiveContent:
Other coders may feel that the code they write can help others. JavaScript libraries contain code for public use.

For it to be helpful, these libraries should be accessible.

lessons.title: CDN
lessons.interactiveContent:
Libraries are usually stored in Content Delivery Network (CDN). CDN is a network that delivers web content quickly by serving it from a nearby server.

We can use a library CDN by including it in the src attribute of the script tag from our HTML file.

Make sure to pick src.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A Content Delivery Network (CDN) can store libraries and deliver web content quickly from a nearby server.

We can use a library CDN by including it in the src attribute of the script tag from our HTML file.

Make sure to pick script, followed by src.

lessons.title: CDN
lessons.interactiveContent:
The src attribute contains the CDN followed by a / and the name of the library. Identify the CDN and the library from the code below.

https://mimo.org is the CDN and bouncy.js is the libraryhttps://mimo.org is the library and bouncy.js is the CDN

https://mimo.org is the CDN and bouncy.js is the library.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Here, src contains the CDN address, then /, then the library filename.

You switch from bouncy.js to calculations.js on the same CDN. Which src value should you use?

https://mimo.org/calculations.jshttps://calculations.js/mimo.orghttps://mimo.org/bouncy.js

https://mimo.org/calculations.js.

lessons.title: Using libraries in HTML
lessons.interactiveContent:
The bouncy.js library makes the text of elements with ID "bounceText" bounce. In this example, teach.getmimo.com is our CDN.

Add a <script> tag and set the correct value for the src attribute.

Make sure to pick script, followed by src, and finally "https://mimo.org/bouncy.js".
lessons.hardModeContent:
The bouncy.js library makes the text of elements with ID "bounceText" bounce. In this example, mimo.org is our CDN.

Add a <script> tag and set the correct value for the src attribute.

Make sure to pick script, followed by src, and finally "https://mimo.org/bouncy.js".

lessons.title: Question 1
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do libraries help us save time?

We can use a solution that is already written by other codersA librarian will help us tidy up our code

We can use a solution that is already written by other coders.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A team needs a date formatter but does not want to build one from scratch. Why can a library help?

It provides code another developer already wrote for that jobIt automatically organizes every file in the projectIt replaces the need to decide what the app should do

It provides code another developer already wrote for that job.

lessons.title: Question 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does CDN stand for?

Content Delivery NetworkCentral Data Notebook

Content Delivery Network.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You load a library while far from its original server. How can a CDN help deliver it quickly?

It can serve the library from a nearby server.It rewrites the library into fewer lines before running it.It makes the library work without loading any code.

It can serve the library from a nearby server.

lessons.title: JS Libraries
lessons.interactiveContent:
With libraries, we can use the solution that someone else coded to solve a problem we're encountering.

Each library is different. When we use a library, we have to check the documentation to know how to use the functions it provides.

lessons.title: How do I know what functions are there?
lessons.interactiveContent:
Based on the documentation below, which function should we use to convert kilograms to pounds?

kgToLb(weight)lbToKg(weight)gToKg(weight)

Make sure to pick kgToLb(weight).
lessons.hardModeContent:
You used kgToLb(weight). Which documented function reverses that conversion?

lbToKg(weight)kgToLb(weight)gToLb(weight)lbToG(weight)

Make sure to pick lbToKg(weight).

lessons.title: Using libraries
lessons.interactiveContent:
To use code from libraries, we need to find the function from the documentation and use it where we need it.

Print 50 kilograms in pounds using the function we found in the conversion.js library.

Make sure to pick conversion followed by . and then kgToLb, (50).
lessons.hardModeContent:
To use code from libraries, we need to find the function from the documentation and use it where we need it.

Start calls from this library with conversion., followed by the function name and parentheses.

Print 50 kilograms in pounds using the documented function from conversion.js.

Make sure to pick conversion, followed by ., kgToLb, and finally (50).

lessons.title: Using downloaded code
lessons.interactiveContent:
There are plenty of libraries we can use. Here, moment.js allows us to format the date of a historic event using JavaScript.

Which part of the code do you think that the moment.js library provides?

format("DD MMMM YYYY")date

format("DD MMMM YYYY").
lessons.hardModeContent:
There are plenty of libraries we can use. Here, moment.js allows us to format the date of a historic event using JavaScript.

You change only the text passed to format. What are you changing?

How the date is written for display.Which HTML element receives the date.The original date passed to moment.

How the date is written for display.

lessons.title: Using libraries
lessons.interactiveContent:
Another benefit of libraries is that problems are usually quickly fixed by their users. Try the kilogram conversion with a String.

We may think it won't work. However, it's still working because someone else already thought about this case!

Make sure to pick "50".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Library users can help fix problems. This version also accepts numbers written as strings.

Convert the string "50" from kilograms to pounds.

Make sure to pick conversion, followed by kgToLb, and finally "50".

lessons.title: Question 1
lessons.interactiveContent:
How can I know what functions are available in a library?

By checking the documentationJust try your luck and guess

By checking the documentation.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Before calling a function from an unfamiliar library, where should you verify its name and inputs?

The library documentationA guess based on the library filenameThe browser tab title

Make sure to pick The library documentation.

lessons.title: Question 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Aside from saving time, what other benefits do libraries provide us?

Libraries have improvements suggested by other users. Even solutions to problems you might not have thought of!None, you can choose not to use libraries if you don't want to save time

Libraries have improvements suggested by other users. Even solutions to problems you might not have thought of!.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A user adds support for number strings to a conversion library. Other users can now pass "50". What benefit is this?

Users can improve a library to handle more situations.Every app using the library becomes free of all bugs.Each user must write the same fix again in their own app.

Users can improve a library to handle more situations.

lessons.title: Question 3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Libraries are only for HTML and CSS.

False. There are also JS librariesFalse. Libraries are only for CSS

False. There are also JS libraries.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A page uses moment.js to format a date. What kind of reusable code is the page using for that task?

JavaScript code supplied by the library.CSS rules that change the date text.HTML tags that calculate the date format.

JavaScript code supplied by the library.
